FACTION_DESC_WESSEX: 871: Alfred takes the throne while the Danish Great Army is encamped at Reading. Lord of Wessex and Kent. Goal: York.
FACTION_DESC_MERCIA: King Burgred's wealthy Mercia with London. Allied to Wessex – Burgred's wife is Alfred's sister – and paying tribute to the Danes.
FACTION_DESC_NORTHUMBRIA: Egbert I, a king set up by the Danes in Bernicia, around Bamburgh and Carlisle. Defensive play.
FACTION_DESC_VIKINGS: The Danish Great Heathen Army has held Jórvík (York) since 866. A culture of its own: fortified camps, heathen shrines, trading places, bóndi and housecarls. You can ask the King of Denmark for aid – but anger him and he may depose you.
LOCKED_DESC: No diplomacy is possible with this land; it cannot be conquered or crossed.
LOCKED_NOTE: Wales, Scotland and Ireland are locked: no diplomacy with them.

Click a province on the map.

Watchtower on the border: +15 defence.

+1 ship: +6 defence, double strength against Danish raids.

CHR_NEW_GAME: A new game begins. Glory awaits!

CHR_MARCH_LOST: An army was lost on the march (near {0}).
CHR_DANEGELD_RAID: Tribute (gafol) paid to the Danes: 40 silver. No raids for 4 turns.
CHR_AI_REPELLED: {0} attacked {1}, but the attack was repelled.
CHR_WON_BURHS: By 900, five burhs guard the realm – {0} prevails!
CHR_TOWER_BUILT: Watchtower raised on the border at {0}.
EVENT_BAD_HARVEST_DESC: After a wet summer the grain has rotted in the fields. The peasants fear famine.
EVENT_GOOD_HARVEST_DESC: This year's harvest has surpassed all hopes; the barns are groaning with grain.
EVENT_MERCHANT_DESC: Frisian trading ships have landed on the shores of {0}, offering cloth, wine and millstones for grain.
EVENT_WITAN_DESC: The Witan debates whether to raise the land tax assessed on each hide.
EVENT_TREASURE_DESC: A plough has turned up an earthen pot full of Roman coins near {0}.
EVENT_TREASURE_C2: Give a share to the Church
EVENT_PLAGUE_DESC: Murrain and pestilence rage as in 896. The beasts are dying and the people fall sick.
EVENT_PLAGUE_C1: Slaughter and burn the sick beasts
EVENT_PILGRIM_DESC: A holy pilgrim has returned from Rome bearing the Pope's blessing for the king.
EVENT_FIRE_DESC: Fire broke out among the thatched houses of {0}, and half the town has burned.
TIP_MINE:
Silver mine: +8 silver per turn.
Only where silver-bearing lead ore was really mined.
TIP_MINT:
Mint: +5 silver per turn, +5 more with a local silver mine.
Requires a burh, and only where an Anglo-Saxon mint really worked
(under Æthelstan's law, coin could only be struck in a town).
TIP_NAVAL_ATTACK:
Besides your neighbouring provinces, your harbours can attack by ship
any coastal or riverside target.
Each ship carries 3 units; on defeat each fleet loses a ship.
REASON_NO_SILVER: There was no silver deposit in this land.
CHR_MINT_BUILT: A mint began striking coin in {0}.
CHR_NAVAL_VICTORY: Victory from the water! {0} captured. ({1} vs {2})
RULER_UNDER_WESSEX: no ruler of its own – held by the King of Wessex
RULER_EA_COIN_KINGS: Æthelred and Oswald, coin-striking kings under the Danes
HIST_871: The "year of battles": Ashdown, Basing and Meretun. After King Æthelred dies, his brother Alfred takes the throne of Wessex.
HIST_872: The Great Heathen Army winters in London; the Mercians pay the Danes tribute.
HIST_873: The Danish army winters at Torksey in Lindsey.
HIST_874: At Repton the Danes drive out King Burgred of Mercia, who flees to Rome; Ceolwulf II is set in his place.
HIST_875: Halfdan marches into Northumbria, Guthrum to Cambridge. Alfred fights seven Danish ships at sea.
HIST_876: Halfdan shares out the lands of Northumbria among his men; Guthrum's army slips into Wareham.
HIST_877: The Danes move to Exeter; a storm off Swanage wrecks 120 of their ships. Mercia is partitioned.
HIST_878: After Twelfth Night Guthrum surprises Chippenham; Alfred flees to the marshes of Athelney, then wins at Edington in spring. Guthrum is baptised.
HIST_879: Guthrum's army moves from Chippenham to Cirencester.
HIST_880: Guthrum's army settles in East Anglia and shares out the land.
HIST_882: Alfred's fleet fights the crews of four Danish ships and captures two.
HIST_885: Alfred relieves the siege of Rochester; his fleet defeats sixteen Danish ships at the mouth of the Stour.
HIST_886: Alfred occupies London and entrusts it to Æthelred of Mercia; all the English not under Danish rule submit to him.
HIST_890: Guthrum, Danish king of East Anglia, dies.
HIST_892: A new Danish army comes from Francia: 250 ships land in Kent at Appledore.
HIST_893: Battles at Farnham and Buttington; the Danes besiege Exeter.
HIST_894: The Danes shelter within the deserted Roman walls of Chester.
HIST_895: The Danes build a fort on the River Lea above London.
HIST_896: Alfred has new warships built, larger than the Danes'; the Danish army disperses.
HIST_899: Alfred the Great dies on 26 October; his son Edward the Elder succeeds him.
HIST_900: Æthelwold, Alfred's nephew, rebels and flees to the Northumbrian Danes, who accept him as king.
HIST_902: Battle of the Holme: Æthelwold and Eohric, Danish king of East Anglia, are killed.
HIST_907: Æthelflæd has the walls of Chester rebuilt.
HIST_909: Edward's army ravages Northumbria; the relics of St Oswald are brought to Gloucester.
HIST_910: At Tettenhall the English defeat the Northumbrian Danes.
HIST_911: Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians, dies; his widow Æthelflæd rules. Edward takes London and Oxford.
HIST_913: Æthelflæd builds burhs at Tamworth and Stafford.
HIST_917: Æthelflæd captures Derby; Edward brings East Anglia to submission.
HIST_918: Æthelflæd enters Leicester and York offers her allegiance; she dies at Tamworth in June.
HIST_919: Ragnall seizes York; Edward takes direct rule of Mercia.
HIST_920: At Bakewell the northern lords all acknowledge Edward as overlord.
HIST_924: Edward the Elder dies; his son Æthelstan becomes king.
HIST_927: Æthelstan takes York: the first king of all the English people.
HIST_934: Æthelstan leads a campaign into Scotland.
HIST_937: Battle of Brunanburh: Æthelstan defeats the alliance of the Scots, Strathclyde and the Dublin Vikings.
HIST_939: Æthelstan dies; Edmund I succeeds. Olaf Guthfrithson seizes York.
HIST_942: Edmund recovers the Five Boroughs: Derby, Leicester, Lincoln, Nottingham and Stamford.
HIST_944: Edmund drives the Norse kings out of York.
HIST_946: Edmund I is murdered at Pucklechurch; his brother Eadred takes the throne.
HIST_948: Eadred burns Ripon; York takes in Eric Bloodaxe.
HIST_954: Eric Bloodaxe falls at Stainmore: Northumbria becomes part of England for good.
HIST_959: On Eadwig's death Edgar becomes king of all England.

FACTION_DESC_EAST_ANGLIA: In 869 the Danish army killed King Edmund, later a saint; since then Æthelred and Oswald strike coin under Danish overlordship. Rich harbours – Gipeswic – but few warriors.
TIP_CHURCH:
Church building: gives stability and silver, more at every level.
Chapel → Small church → Church → Minster → Basilica → Cathedral.
A basilica needs a burh; a cathedral needs a former bishop's see.
TIP_CHURCH_NEXT: Next level – {0}: +{1} stability and +{2} silver per turn.
TIP_BARRACKS:
Military building: recruits are raised here; each level musters more men and adds defence.
Barracks → Armoury → Thegns' hall → Housecarl quarters (needs a burh).
REASON_NO_SEE: A cathedral can only be built at a former bishop's see.
REASON_NEEDS_BARRACKS: Recruiting requires barracks in this province.
TIP_BARRACKS_NEXT: Next level – {0}: +{1} fyrd / +{2} thegn per recruitment, +{3} defence.

INV_1015_CNUT: Cnut's Danish army lands on the coast of Wessex – target: {0}.

MILESTONE_YORK:
{0} has taken York, the rich city of the northern kingdom.
The game goes on – the Danes and Norwegians may yet return.
MILESTONE_EIGHT: {0} rules eight provinces: the greater part of England is in your hands.
MILESTONE_ALL:
{0} has united all England!

RULER_UNDER_NORMANS: no ruler of its own – held by the Norman king

RULER_HARALD_BLUETOOTH: Harald Bluetooth, King of the Danes
RULER_HARALD_II_DK: Harald II, King of the Danes
RULER_MAGNUS: Magnus the Good, King of Denmark and Norway
RULER_SWEYN_ESTRIDSEN: Sweyn Estridsen, King of the Danes

RULER_CANUTE_IV: Canute IV (the Saint), King of the Danes
RULER_OLAF_I_DK: Olaf I, King of the Danes
HIST_973: Edgar is crowned at Bath; at Chester six kings row him on the Dee in token of submission.
HIST_978: King Edward the Martyr is murdered at Corfe; his brother Æthelred takes the throne.
HIST_991: Battle of Maldon: Ealdorman Byrhtnoth falls against the Vikings; for the first time England pays tribute (gafol) – 10,000 pounds.
HIST_1002: On St Brice's Day, at Æthelred's order, the Danes living in England are massacred.
HIST_1013: Sweyn Forkbeard conquers England; Æthelred flees to Normandy.
HIST_1016: Battle of Assandun: Cnut defeats Edmund Ironside and after Edmund's death becomes king of all England.
HIST_1042: Edward the Confessor becomes King of England.
HIST_1065: The Northumbrians rise against Earl Tostig; Westminster Abbey is consecrated.
HIST_1066: Edward the Confessor dies; Harold defeats Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge, then falls at Hastings against William's army.
HIST_1086: William the Conqueror has the great survey of the realm made: the Domesday Book.
CHR_REVOLT: {0} rose in revolt and went over to {1} ({2} lost it).
CHR_REVOLT_OURS: {0} rose against us and went over to {1}!
CHR_REVOLT_JOINED: The people of {0} rose against their lords and joined us!
CHR_STABILITY_REVOLT: Order collapsed: {0} broke away from the kingdom. The Witan calms tempers.
CHR_STABILITY_RIOTS: Riots broke out: half the army scattered, but the kingdom endures.
EVENT_KIND_FOLLOWUP: The consequence of an earlier decision
EVENT_OUTCOME_FAIL: Our decision – “{0}” – has gone badly wrong.
EVENT_FEUD_DESC: Two thegnly kindreds have sworn a blood feud in {0}. Paying the wergild could bring peace.
EVENT_FEUD_C3: Take one side into our service
EVENT_OUTLAWS_DESC: Brigands are robbing merchants in the woods of {0}.
EVENT_OUTLAWS_C2: Pardon them if they take up arms for us
EVENT_RELICS_DESC: A wandering monk offers to sell the bones of a martyr to the church of {0}.
EVENT_SHIPWRECK_DESC: A storm has driven a merchant ship ashore near {0}. Its cargo lies scattered on the strand.
EVENT_SHIPWRECK_C1: By right of wreck it is ours
EVENT_WOLVES_DESC: In the hard winter, wolf packs are attacking the flocks around {0}.
EVENT_MINT_REFORM_DESC: The moneyers propose to recoin all silver at a single weight bearing the king's image – as Edgar did in 973.
EVENT_BISHOP_DEMAND_DESC: The Church asks the king for a grant of land and the strict collection of tithes.
EVENT_EALDORMAN_POWER_DESC: One of the ealdormen demands more land and judicial rights in his shire.
EVENT_THEGN_REWARD_DESC: The king's thegns ask for bookland granted by charter in return for their faithful service.
EVENT_SHIPS_SIGHTED_DESC: Dragon-prowed ships have been sighted off the coast of {0}. Perhaps they will sail on – perhaps not.
EVENT_MERCENARIES_DESC: The leader of a Danish fleet – like Thorkell the Tall in 1012 – offers to fight on our side for silver.
EVENT_FAIR_DESC: The merchants of {0} ask for a royal licence to hold a yearly fair.
EVENT_FLOOD_DESC: The river has burst its banks near {0}, drowning the meadows and the mills.
EVENT_SCHOLAR_DESC: A learned monk – like Asser at Alfred's court – offers to translate Latin books into English.
EVENT_HORSES_DESC: Frankish horse dealers have brought fine warhorses to the market of {0}.
EVENT_COMET_DESC: A long-haired star has appeared in the sky. The people whisper fearfully of great changes.
EVENT_GOSPEL_BOOK_DESC: The monks of {0} would make a gilded gospel book if the king pays for the vellum and pigments.
EVENT_SPY_DESC: We have caught an enemy spy disguised as a travelling merchant.
EVENT_WEDDING_OFFER_DESC: An envoy has come from the court of {0}: {1} would gladly give a kinswoman in marriage to our royal house.
EVENT_WAREHAM_OATH_DESC: The Danish army has withdrawn into Wareham and, swearing on their holy ring, offers peace and hostages. Can we trust their oath?
EVENT_WAREHAM_OATH_C2: Do not trust them – stay under arms
EVENT_ATHELNEY_DESC: After Twelfth Night Guthrum fell upon Chippenham. The king fled with a handful of followers into the marshes of Athelney. What shall we do?
EVENT_ATHELNEY_C1: Hide and gather the army in secret
EVENT_EDINGTON_DESC: After seven weeks in hiding, the men of Somerset, Wiltshire and Hampshire gather around their king at Egbert's Stone. The time for Edington has come.
EVENT_EDMUND_MARTYR_DESC: King Edmund, slain by the Danes in 869, is revered by the people as a saint, and miracles are told at his tomb.
EVENT_GUTHRUM_BAPTISM_DESC: The English demand that Guthrum be baptised at Aller, taking the Christian name Æthelstan.
EVENT_LONDON_RESTORED_DESC: The trading town of Lundenwic is deserted. Within the old Roman walls a new town could rise, as Alfred did in 886.
EVENT_LONDON_RESTORED_C2: Entrust the town to an ealdorman
EVENT_BURGHAL_HIDAGE_DESC: By the Burghal Hidage, every pole of wall needs four men. Shall we build a network of forts so that no one lives more than a day's march from a burh?
EVENT_AETHELFLAED_BURHS_DESC: Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, is raising burhs from Bridgnorth to Warwick. Shall we follow her example?
EVENT_BRUNANBURH_DESC: Olaf of Dublin, Constantine of the Scots and the Britons of Strathclyde have invaded with a great host. Æthelstan summons every Englishman to battle.
EVENT_MALDON_GAFOL_DESC: Ealdorman Byrhtnoth has fallen at Maldon. Archbishop Sigeric advises paying the Danes a gafol of 10,000 pounds.
EVENT_ST_BRICE_DESC: King Æthelred has ordered that all Danes living in England be slain on 13 November. Shall we carry out the order?
EVENT_SWEYN_REVENGE_DESC: Gunnhild, sister of King Sweyn of Denmark, died in the massacre. Sweyn has sworn revenge, and his ships are bound for {0}.
EVENT_ASSANDUN_DESC: The armies of Edmund Ironside and Cnut face each other at Assandun. Eadric Streona's loyalty wavers.
EVENT_ASSANDUN_C2: Divide the kingdom, as at Olney
EVENT_HAROLD_CHOICE_DESC: Harald Hardrada gathers off the coast of Northumbria while Duke William waits for a fair wind in Normandy. Where shall the army march?
EVENT_COURT_DESC: The king has summoned the Witan at Easter. Decide the policy for the year ahead!
AMBITIONS_TIP: Fulfil ambitions for rewards! A new one takes the place of each fulfilled ambition.
AMB_THEGNS_DESC: Have {0} thegns in total (armies on the march do not count).
AMB_CHURCH_DESC: Raise a church building to level {0}.

REPORT_RAID_CONQUERED: The invaders have seized {0} and taken {1} silver as plunder!
TIP_BURH_NORSE: A fortified camp with bank and palisade, like the Great Army's winter camps at Repton and Torksey: +15 defence, cheaper than a burh.
TIP_FARM_NORSE: Settler village (the Danish -by and -thorpe villages): +8 food per turn.
TIP_PORT_NORSE:
Longphort on the riverbank: +3 silver per turn, longships can be built.
Cheaper than an English harbour.
TIP_SHIP_NORSE:
+1 longship: +6 defence; carries 4 warriors per ship in naval attacks (English ships only 3).
Requires a longphort.
TIP_FYRD_NORSE:
Raise bóndi (free farmer-warriors, the armed strength of the settlers).
Requires a hall; numbers depend on the hall's level.
TIP_THEGN_NORSE:
Raise housecarls (the jarl's professional, paid bodyguard).
Requires a hall; numbers depend on the hall's level.
TIP_BARRACKS_NORSE:
Military building: troops are raised here; each level brings more men and more defence.
Longhouse → Hall → Jarl's hall → Royal hall (requires a fortified camp).
TIP_MINT_NORSE:
Mint: +5 silver per turn. Requires a fortified camp and an old minting place
(the Danish kings of Jórvík – Cnut, Siefred, Sihtric – struck their own silver pennies).
TIP_HOF:
Heathen sacred site: gives stability, and at higher levels improves relations with the king of the homeland.
Vé → Hörgr → Hof → Great hof → Royal sanctuary (the great hof requires a fortified camp).
TIP_HOF_NEXT: Next level – {0}: +{1} stability and +{2} relations with the homeland per turn.
TIP_MARKET:
Trading place: furs, amber and walrus ivory are traded here for hacksilver – +5 silver per turn.
Coastal or riverside provinces only.
INFO_NO_BARRACKS_NORSE: Military building: no hall (cannot raise troops)
TIP_BARRACKS_NEXT_NORSE: Next level – {0}: +{1} bóndi / +{2} housecarls per levy, +{3} defence.
REASON_NEEDS_BARRACKS_NORSE: Raising troops requires a hall in this province.
REASON_OTHER_CULTURE: Your people do not build this.
CHR_WITAN_GIFT_NORSE: Gifts to the leaders of the thing (20 silver).

AMB_THEGNS_DESC_NORSE: Have {0} housecarls in total (armies on the march do not count).
AMB_HOF_DESC: Raise a sacred site to level {0}.
AMB_HOMELAND_DESC: Reach {0} relations with the king of the homeland.
MILESTONE_BURHS_NORSE: {0} guards its land with five fortified camps.
CHR_MILESTONE_BURHS_NORSE: Milestone: five fortified camps guard the realm.
EVENT_THING_DESC: The free warriors have gathered at the spring thing to make law. What shall be the order of the year?
EVENT_THING_C3: Send envoys and gifts to the homeland
EVENT_FEUD_DESC_NORSE: Two kindreds have sworn a blood feud in {0}. Paying the blood price could bring peace.
EVENT_FEUD_C1_NORSE: The jarl pays the blood price
EVENT_TREASURE_C2_NORSE: Offer a share to the gods
EVENT_HOMELAND_ENVOY_DESC: An envoy of the king of the homeland has arrived: his lord demands a share of the plunder his kinsmen have won.
EVENT_EXILED_JARL_DESC: A jarl exiled from the homeland has landed with his warriors on the shores of {0} and offers his service.
EVENT_EXILED_JARL_C2: Hand him over to the king
EVENT_SKALD_DESC: An Icelandic skald would compose a drápa, a praise poem of our deeds – it would be recited at the royal court of the homeland too.
EVENT_HOMELAND_WAR_DESC: The king of the homeland is at war with his neighbours and asks us for housecarls.
EVENT_BLOT_DESC: Yule is near. The people expect a great sacrificial feast (blót), as the forefathers kept it.
EVENT_SETTLERS_DESC: Families from the homeland ask for land in {0} to settle.
EVENT_MISSIONARY_DESC: An English priest preaches the faith of Christ among the settlers of {0}, and more and more listen to him.
EVENT_VIKING_EXPEDITION_DESC: Young warriors from the shores of {0} want to sail to Frankia or Ireland for plunder.
EVENT_THING_DISPUTE_DESC: At the thing, old warriors and new settlers quarrel over the land of {0}.
EVENT_HALFDAN_SETTLES_DESC: “Halfdan shared out the land of the Northumbrians, and they began to plough” – so says the chronicle for 876. The army is weary of campaigning. Shall we settle?
EVENT_ST_PETER_COINAGE_DESC: The moneyers of Jórvík would strike a new penny. The archbishop proposes the name of St Peter; the warriors want Thor's hammer and the sword.
EVENT_ERIC_BLOODAXE_DESC: Eric Bloodaxe, driven out of Norway, has arrived with his ships and claims the throne of Jórvík. A great warrior – but the Danish king dislikes him.
EVENT_BLUETOOTH_CONVERSION_DESC: Harald Bluetooth, King of Denmark, has been baptised and has carved on the Jelling stone that he made the Danes Christian. Shall we follow his example?
EVENT_SWEYN_CALL_DESC: King Sweyn has sailed with a great fleet to conquer England and calls every Dane living here to his side.
HOMELAND_BUTTON_TIP: Ask the King of {0} for warriors or a raid, or send him gifts.
HOMELAND_OFFER_WARRIORS: Warriors: {0} bóndi, {1} housecarls and {2} longships – landing in {3}.
HOMELAND_OFFER_RAID: A raid on our enemies' coasts (strength {0}) – the plunder is ours.
HOMELAND_OFFER_RAID_CONQUEST: A conquering host on our enemies' coasts (strength {0}) – if it wins, the land is ours too.
HOMELAND_FLEET_ON_WAY: Under way: a fleet bound for {0}, arriving in {1}.
HOMELAND_WAIT: You can ask for aid again in {0}.
HOMELAND_BTN_RAID: Ask for a raid on our enemies
HOMELAND_WARRIORS_TIP:
If the king agrees, the warriors land in one of your coastal provinces.
He expects service in return (−12 relations); if he refuses: −5.
HOMELAND_RAID_TIP:
If the king agrees, raiders strike an enemy coastal province and the plunder goes to you.
Above 75 relations he sends a conquering host.
HOMELAND_NO_TARGET: You are not at war with anyone who holds a coastal or riverside province.
HOMELAND_REASON_COOLDOWN: The king is still considering your last request – wait a little.
HOMELAND_REASON_NO_COAST: You have no coastal or riverside province where the ships could land.
HOMELAND_REASON_NO_TARGET: You are not at war with anyone who holds a coastal or riverside province.
HOMELAND_REFUSED: {0} has refused: “Win your land yourselves!” (−5 relations)
HOMELAND_WARRIORS_SENT: {0} has agreed! {1} bóndi, {2} housecarls and {3} longships have set sail for {4}; they land in {5}.
HOMELAND_RAID_SENT: {0} has agreed! Raiders have fallen upon the coasts of {1} (strength {2}).
HOMELAND_RAID_PENDING: The defenders are still deciding how to meet them.
HOMELAND_RAID_REPELLED: But the defenders drove the raiders off.
HOMELAND_RAID_LOOT: The raid succeeded: {0} silver of plunder is in our treasury!
HOMELAND_RAID_GAFOL: The defenders chose to pay gafol: {0} silver is ours.
HOMELAND_RAID_CONQUERED: The conquering host has seized {0} and taken {1} silver as plunder!
CHR_HOMELAND_FLEET: {0} sent a fleet to {1}: {2} bóndi, {3} housecarls.
CHR_HOMELAND_ARRIVED: The fleet from the homeland has landed at {0} (+{1} bóndi, +{2} housecarls, +{3} longships).
CHR_HOMELAND_FLEET_LOST: The fleet from the homeland found no friendly shore and turned for home.
CHR_HOMELAND_GIFT: Gifts to the king of the homeland: {0} ({1} silver).
CHR_HOMELAND_LOOT: Plunder from the homeland's raid ({0}): {1} silver.
CHR_HOMELAND_GAFOL: {0} paid gafol to the raiders: {1} silver is ours.
FACTION_DESC_NORWEGIANS: The Norse sea-kings of Dublin, Man and Orkney, lords of the Irish Sea and the Isles. Scattered islands and a strong fleet; the King of Norway may send aid – but anger him and he sends a punitive fleet to depose you.
FACTION_DESC_NORMANS: The Seine Vikings are settling around Rouen; in 911 Rollo receives Normandy from the Frankish king. A culture of its own: motte-and-bailey castles, knights (stronger than thegns), abbeys – and in 1066 the great conquest may come.
FACTION_DESC_WALES: The Celtic kingdoms of Gwynedd, Powys, Dyfed and Morgannwg behind Offa's Dyke. A poor land, but in their hills they defend 25% harder; the war with Mercia is ancient. The land of clas monasteries, the llys and the bards.
WITAN_NORMANS_3: Poppa, daughter of the Count of Bayeux
WITAN_NORWEGIANS_3: Ketill Flatnose, lord of the Isles
WITAN_WALES_2: Hyfaidd ap Bledri, King of Dyfed
WITAN_WALES_3: Meurig ap Arthfael, King of Gwent
RULER_SEINE_VIKINGS: the leaders of the Seine Vikings (Sidroc, Weland)
RULER_DUBLIN_EXILE: the kings expelled from Dublin in 902, in exile
RULER_GODRED_CROVAN: Godred Crovan, King of Man and the Isles
RULER_RHODRI_AP_MERFYN: Rhodri ap Merfyn, King of Gwynedd
RULER_GRUFFYDD_AP_LLYWELYN: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn, King of all Wales
RULER_HAAKON_GOOD: Haakon the Good, King of Norway
RULER_OLAF_SAINT: Olaf II (St Olaf), King of Norway
RULER_OLAF_KYRRE: Olaf III (the Peaceful), King of Norway
HOMELAND_WRATH_WARNING: Beware! If relations fall below {0}, the king may send a punitive fleet against your seat – and if it wins, he will depose you.
HOMELAND_ANGRY_DESC: {0} is angry with us. If relations worsen, he will send a fleet to depose us. Send gifts, or do his bidding!
CHR_HOMELAND_ANGRY: The wrath of {0} grows against us.
CHR_RAID_PUNISH: A punitive host has landed before {0} (strength {1})!
RAID_PUNISH_SUBMIT_LINE: You may submit: for {0} silver the king shows mercy, and relations improve.
RAID_PUNISH_WARNING: If the defenders fall, {0} will set a new lord over {1} – your reign will end!
CHR_PUNISH_FLEET: {0} has sent a punitive fleet against {1} (strength {2})!
CHR_PUNISH_SUBMITTED: We submitted to the king of the homeland, {0} ({1} silver).
CHR_PUNISH_REPELLED: We threw back the punitive expedition of {0} at {1}! The king must respect our strength.
CHR_DEPOSED_WORLD: {0} deposed the ruler of {1} and set a new jarl over {2}.
DEPOSED_DESC: The host of {0} has taken the hall of {1}. The king has set a new jarl in your place – your reign is over.
TIP_BURH_NORMAN: Motte-and-bailey castle: an earthen mound with a timber tower and palisade – +25 defence (a burh gives only +20).
TIP_FARM_NORMAN: Manor with villein villages and a mill: +8 food per turn.
TIP_FYRD_NORMAN:
Raise foot soldiers (pedites: spearmen and archers).
Requires stables; numbers depend on their level.
TIP_THEGN_NORMAN:
Raise knights (milites): armoured horsemen, strength 14 (a thegn is 12).
Requires stables; numbers depend on their level.
TIP_BARRACKS_NORMAN:
Military building: troops are raised here; each level brings more men and more defence.
Stables → Armoury → Knights' hall → Ducal stables (requires a motte castle).
INFO_NO_BARRACKS_NORMAN: Military building: no stables (cannot raise troops)
TIP_BARRACKS_NEXT_NORMAN: Next level – {0}: +{1} foot / +{2} knights per levy, +{3} defence.
REASON_NEEDS_BARRACKS_NORMAN: Raising troops requires stables in this province.
REPORT_ATTACK_WON_NORMAN:
Our army ({1}) has defeated the defenders of {0} ({2}).

Our losses: {3} foot, {4} knights
Enemy losses: {5} foot, {6} heavy troops
Marched in as garrison: {7} foot, {8} knights
REPORT_ATTACK_LOST_NORMAN:
The defenders of {0} ({2}) have thrown back our assault ({1}).

Our losses: {3} foot, {4} knights
Enemy losses: {5} warriors
CHR_WITAN_GIFT_NORMAN: Gifts to the barons of the ducal council (20 silver).
EVENT_COURT_DESC_NORMAN: At Easter the duke has summoned his barons and bishops to Fécamp. What shall be the policy for the year?
AMB_THEGNS_DESC_NORMAN: Have {0} knights in total (armies on the march do not count).
MILESTONE_BURHS_NORMAN: {0} rules its land with five motte castles.
CHR_MILESTONE_BURHS_NORMAN: Milestone: five motte castles guard the duchy.
TIP_BURH_WELSH: Dinas: a hill fort with stone and earth ramparts, like Dinas Emrys – +20 defence.
TIP_FARM_WELSH: Hafod and hendre: summer and winter pastures for the cattle – +8 food per turn.
TIP_FYRD_WELSH:
Raise the llu (the host): free spearmen and archers.
Requires a llys; numbers depend on its level.
TIP_THEGN_WELSH:
Raise warriors of the teulu, the king's sworn warband.
Requires a llys; numbers depend on its level.
TIP_BARRACKS_WELSH:
Military building: troops are raised here; each level brings more men and more defence.
Tref → Llys → Great llys → Royal llys (requires a dinas).
INFO_NO_BARRACKS_WELSH: Military building: no llys (cannot raise troops)
TIP_BARRACKS_NEXT_WELSH: Next level – {0}: +{1} llu / +{2} teulu per levy, +{3} defence.
REASON_NEEDS_BARRACKS_WELSH: Raising troops requires a llys in this province.
REPORT_ATTACK_WON_WELSH:
Our army ({1}) has defeated the defenders of {0} ({2}).

Our losses: {3} llu, {4} teulu
Enemy losses: {5} foot, {6} heavy troops
Marched in as garrison: {7} llu, {8} teulu
REPORT_ATTACK_LOST_WELSH:
The defenders of {0} ({2}) have thrown back our assault ({1}).

Our losses: {3} llu, {4} teulu
Enemy losses: {5} warriors
CHR_WITAN_GIFT_WELSH: Gifts to the nobles of the llys (20 silver).
TIP_CHURCH_WELSH:
Holy site: gives stability and silver, more at every level.
Llan → Small church → Clas → Great clas → Mam-eglwys → Bishop's cathedral.
The mam-eglwys requires a dinas; the cathedral an old bishop's see.
EVENT_COURT_DESC_WELSH: At Easter the king has summoned his nobles and the abbots of the clasau. What shall be the policy for the year?
AMB_THEGNS_DESC_WELSH: Have {0} teulu warriors in total (armies on the march do not count).
MILESTONE_BURHS_WELSH: {0} guards its valleys with five hill forts.
CHR_MILESTONE_BURHS_WELSH: Milestone: five dinasoedd guard the valleys of Wales.
EVENT_BARDS_DESC: The bards (beirdd) have gathered at the king's court to compete with praise poems for the bardic chair.
EVENT_BARDS_C1: Offer a prize to the winner
EVENT_BARDS_C2: We have no time for songs
EVENT_CATTLE_RAID_DESC: The young warriors want to go on a cattle raid (preiddiau) across the border from {0}.
EVENT_OFFAS_DYKE_DESC: King Offa's great bank is crumbling in {0}. Shall we strengthen it, or trust the hills to defend us?
EVENT_OFFAS_DYKE_C2: Let the llu guard the passes
EVENT_HERMIT_SAINT_DESC: A holy hermit wishes to found a cell (llan) in the valleys of {0}, as St David once did.
EVENT_ABBEY_FOUNDATION_DESC: An abbey burned by the Vikings – like Jumièges – could be refounded in {0}.
EVENT_LANDLESS_KNIGHTS_DESC: Younger sons of barons – like the sons of Tancred of Hauteville – seek their fortune and offer their service in {0}.
EVENT_PEACE_OF_GOD_DESC: The bishops proclaim the Peace of God: none may attack clergy or peasants, nor anyone on holy days.
EVENT_PEACE_OF_GOD_C2: The knights will not be bound
EVENT_HEBRIDES_TRIBUTE_DESC: The islanders of the Hebrides and {0} are reluctant to pay the sea-kings' tribute.
EVENT_IRISH_KINGS_DESC: The Irish kings of Leinster and Brega are gathering a host against Dublin.
EVENT_SIEGE_OF_PARIS_DESC: Sigfred sails against Paris with seven hundred ships and calls the Seine Vikings too. Shall we join?
EVENT_SAINT_CLAIR_TREATY_DESC: King Charles the Simple offers Rouen and its lands to Rollo, if he is baptised and defends the Seine against other Vikings.
EVENT_BATTLE_OF_VARAVILLE_DESC: King Henry I of France and the Count of Anjou invade Normandy. At the ford of the Dives the rising tide splits their army in two.
EVENT_CONQUEST_PLAN_DESC: Edward the Confessor is dead, and Harold Godwinson has broken his oath. Shall we build a fleet at the mouth of the Dives and cross to England?
EVENT_HEREFORD_TRIBUTE_DESC: Æthelstan has summoned the Welsh kings to Hereford and demands a yearly tribute of gold, silver and cattle.
EVENT_ARMES_PRYDEIN_DESC: The prophecy “Armes Prydein” foretells that the Welsh, Scots, Irish and Dublin Norse will together drive out the Saxons. A great alliance is forming.
EVENT_HYWEL_DDA_LAWS_DESC: Hywel Dda would summon the judges of every cantref to Tŷ Gwyn at Whitland to set down a single book of laws.
EVENT_GRUFFYDD_RAID_DESC: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn, allied with Earl Ælfgar, prepares to burn Hereford.
EVENT_HAFRSFJORD_DESC: Harald Fairhair has defeated the petty kings of Norway at Hafrsfjord. The beaten chieftains flee west to the Isles.
EVENT_ORKNEY_EARLDOM_DESC: Harald Fairhair would grant Orkney as an earldom to the kin of Rögnvald of Møre. Shall we accept the king's man?
EVENT_CLONTARF_DESC: Brian Boru, High King of all Ireland, marches on Dublin. Sigtrygg Silkbeard calls warriors from Orkney and Man.
EVENT_OLAF_TRYGGVASON_DESC: King Olaf Tryggvason has sailed to the Isles and offers the jarls a choice: baptism or death.
EVENT_HARDRADA_CALL_DESC: Harald Hardrada sails with three hundred ships for the throne of England and calls the warriors of the Isles to his side.
